Let me analyze each statement based on molecular orbital theory:

A. "Any orbital can accommodate up to two electrons, so buta-1,3-diene has eight π electrons"
- According to the Pauli exclusion principle, an orbital can accommodate a maximum of 2 electrons with opposite spins.
- Buta-1,3-diene (CH₂=CH-CH=CH₂) has 4 carbon atoms with conjugated double bonds.
- Each carbon in the double bond contributes one p orbital electron to the π system.
- With 4 carbon atoms participating in the π system, there are 4 electrons in the π system.
- This statement is incorrect because buta-1,3-diene has 4 π electrons, not 8.

B. "Some orbitals do not have any nodes"
- This is correct. The lowest energy orbitals (like 1s orbitals) have zero nodes.

C. "The π molecular orbitals of buta-1,3-diene are derived from 2p atomic orbitals of carbon atoms, and there are four of them"
- This is correct. The π molecular orbitals in buta-1,3-diene are formed from the 2p atomic orbitals of the 4 carbon atoms, resulting in 4 π molecular orbitals.

D. "The complete set of molecular orbitals obtained by combining atomic orbitals includes an increased number of nodes"
- This is correct. As molecular orbitals form from atomic orbitals, the number of nodes generally increases with energy level.

Based on this analysis, statement A is incorrect. Buta-1,3-diene has 4 π electrons (one from each carbon in the π system), not 8 as claimed.
